title: Cofinal poset-nerve replacement of a kappa-small simplicial set
statement:
Use the universes, infinite regular cardinals and $\kappa$-small simplicial sets of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and simplicial sets, ordinary nerves, quasicategories, functor simplicial sets, constant diagrams $\Delta_K$, right-pinched mapping spaces and coherent cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal and let $K$ be a $\kappa$-small simplicial set; $K$ need not be a quasicategory. There exist a partially ordered set $B$ with $|B|<\kappa$ (so $B$ is finite when $\kappa=\aleph_0$) and a simplicial map $\varphi:N(B)\to K$ with the following property. For every quasicategory $\mathcal E$ in a sufficiently large universe, every simplicial map $p:K\to\mathcal E$ and every vertex $T$ of $\mathcal E$, restriction along $\varphi$ induces an equivalence of Kan complexes
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_KT)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(B),\mathcal E)}(p\varphi,\Delta_{N(B)}T).$$
In particular, every coherent cocone $p\varphi\to\Delta_{N(B)}T$ is joined by a path in the target to the restriction of a coherent cocone $p\to\Delta_KT$. The case $K=\varnothing$ is included, and then $B=\varnothing$. No existence of colimits in $\mathcal E$ is assumed.

source.place: Variant 4.2.3.15 (kappa uncountable; the poset is kappa-small because each of the five categories of simplices built from a kappa-small simplicial set has fewer than kappa objects and morphisms, kappa being uncountable regular) and Variant 4.2.3.16 (K finite, finite poset), printed pp. 255-256, with Proposition 4.1.1.8 (1)=>(2) (printed pp. 225-226) and the join/cocone comparison of Proposition 4.2.1.5 for the mapping-space form; as used in Remark 5.3.1.12. Read 2026-10-17 from the online PDF; not archived in literature/ (WANTED). No Stacks tag states it.

proof.text: For a map $u:A\to Z$, write $R_u$ for restriction on the displayed cocone mapping spaces in the statement. For composable maps $u:A\to Z$ and $w:Z\to W$, the defining precomposition formula gives $R_{wu}=R_uR_w$ (with the intervening diagram restricted to $Z$). Thus a composite of maps having the universal cocone-restriction property has that property: each composite on components and on all based homotopy groups is a composite of isomorphisms. The spaces concerned are Kan even for an arbitrary indexing simplicial set by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. If $K=\varnothing$, take $B=\varnothing$ and $\varphi$ the unique map. Both indexing shapes are identical and restriction is the identity, so all clauses hold. In the remainder suppose $K\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: HTT Variant 4.2.3.15, composition of five maps, and Variant 4.2.3.16, empty base case; elementary restriction calculation. Online primary source read 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag is asserted.

proof.text: We first give the common degeneracy-removal argument. Suppose $X$ is a small simplicial set every nondegenerate simplex of which is a monomorphism. Let $\mathsf S(X)$ be its simplex category, as explicitly defined in [lem-coef-simplex-last-vertex-cocone-equivalence], and let $B_X$ be its full subcategory of nondegenerate simplices. An arrow into a nondegenerate simplex is uniquely determined by its composite into $X$, since that target simplex is degreewise injective. Between nondegenerate simplices its simplex operator must be injective: a nontrivial surjective factor would make its source degenerate. Consequently there is at most one arrow between any two objects of $B_X$. Ordering them by existence of this arrow is antisymmetric, since arrows in both directions force equal dimensions and hence identity monotone operators. Thus $B_X$ is a poset. By [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition], every simplex $\sigma$ has a unique presentation $\sigma=\bar\sigma\Delta(s_\sigma)$ with $s_\sigma$ surjective and $\bar\sigma$ nondegenerate. For any arrow $\alpha:\sigma\to\tau$ with $\tau$ nondegenerate, factor $\alpha=t_\alpha\circ s_\alpha$ as its surjective image factor $s_\alpha:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$ followed by its injective image inclusion $t_\alpha:[r]\hookrightarrow[m]$. The simplex $\tau\Delta(t_\alpha)$ is nondegenerate: it is a monomorphism, and a degenerate simplex cannot be degreewise injective. Uniqueness of nondegenerate decomposition applied to $\sigma=\tau\Delta(t_\alpha)\Delta(s_\alpha)$ now gives $s_\alpha=s_\sigma$ and $\tau\Delta(t_\alpha)=\bar\sigma$. This is the unique factorization $\sigma\xrightarrow{s_\sigma}\bar\sigma\xrightarrow{t_\alpha}\tau$. Hence $(\sigma\downarrow B_X)$ has the initial object $(\bar\sigma,s_\sigma)$. The natural transformation from the constant functor at this object to the identity contracts its nerve by [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence]. To identify the infinity-categorical comma used below, put $C=\mathsf S(X)$. The nerve $N(C_{\sigma/})\to N(C)$ is an isofibration: composition in an ordinary category fills all inner horns, and an isomorphism $t:c\to c\prime$ lifts at an object $\sigma\to c$ by composition to $\sigma\to c\prime$, with its inverse lifting the inverse isomorphism. The strict pullback $N(B_X)\times_{N(C)}N(C_{\sigma/})$ is exactly the nerve of the ordinary comma just contracted. By [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit], this strict pullback computes the infinity-categorical pullback in [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-comma-criterion]. Thus its comma hypothesis holds for the nerve of $i_X:B_X\hookrightarrow\mathsf S(X)$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-comma-criterion] to get the universal equivalence $R_{N(i_X)}$ on cocone mapping spaces. Both index objects are nerves of small ordinary categories; no quasicategory assertion about $X$ was used.

proof.text: Assume first that $\kappa>\aleph_0$. Put $I_1=\mathsf S(K)$ and $K_1=N(I_1)$. The explicit last-vertex map $a=\ell_K:K_1\to K$ has universal cocone-restriction equivalences by [lem-coef-simplex-last-vertex-cocone-equivalence]. Put $I_2=\mathsf S(K_1)$ and $K_2=N(I_2^{\mathrm{op}})$. The first-vertex map $b=N(v_{I_1}):K_2\to K_1$ has the same property by [lem-coef-simplex-first-vertex-cocone-equivalence]. Here the opposite on $I_2$ is essential: a simplex operator $\alpha$ gives the arrow from the first vertex of the target chain to vertex $\alpha(0)$, so it has the claimed direction only after taking the opposite.

source.place: HTT Variant 4.2.3.15, steps (1) and (2), printed p. 255. Online primary source read 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag is asserted.

proof.text: Let $I_3=\mathsf S_{\mathrm{inj}}(K_1)$, retaining ALL simplices of $K_1$ as objects and only injective simplex operators as arrows. Set $X=N(I_3^{\mathrm{op}})$, and let $c:X\to K_2$ be the nerve of inclusion. Its restriction maps $R_c$ are equivalences by [lem-coef-injective-simplex-cocone-restriction]. Every nonidentity morphism of $I_3$ strictly increases the dimension of its object: an injective monotone self-map of $[n]$ is the identity. A nondegenerate simplex of $X$ is therefore a chain of nonidentity arrows whose object-dimensions strictly decrease. Its vertices are distinct. The associated map $\Delta^r\to X$ is degreewise injective: equality of two image simplices implies equality of their vertex strings, and distinctness of the original vertices implies equality of the two monotone indexing maps. Thus every nondegenerate simplex of $X$ is a monomorphism.

source.place: HTT Variant 4.2.3.15, step (3) and the dimension/face observation in step (5). Online primary source read 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag is asserted.

proof.text:
Apply the degeneracy-removal argument of step 2 to this $X$, and write $B=B_X$. Let $d=\ell_X:N(\mathsf S(X))\to X$; [lem-coef-simplex-last-vertex-cocone-equivalence] gives the equivalence $R_d$. With $e=N(i_X):N(B)\to N(\mathsf S(X))$, step 2 gives the equivalence $R_e$. Define the required actual simplicial map to be
$$\varphi=a\circ b\circ c\circ d\circ e:N(B)\longrightarrow K.$$
For every fixed $\mathcal E,p,T$, restriction along this map is exactly the composite of the five restrictions $R_a,R_b,R_c,R_d,R_e$ applied to their successively restricted diagrams. By step 1 it is an equivalence. This constructs the map and its restriction property before imposing a cardinal estimate; no colimit of $p$ has been chosen.

proof.text: We check $|B|<\kappa$ in the uncountable case. Let $\lambda<\kappa$ be the number of nondegenerate simplices of $K$, and put $\mu=\max(\aleph_0,\lambda)<\kappa$. By [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition], all simplices of $K$ are specified by a nondegenerate simplex and a monotone surjection between finite ordinals. There are countably many such finite operators, so their total number is at most $\mu$. The morphisms of $I_1=\mathsf S(K)$ are specified by two such objects and one of those finite operators, hence also number at most $\mu$. Finite chains of these morphisms, which are the simplices of $K_1$, again number at most $\mu$: for infinite $\mu$, a countable union of finite powers of $\mu$ has cardinality $\mu$. Repeating the same count for the objects and arrows of $I_2$ and its wide subcategory $I_3$, and for finite chains in $I_3^{\mathrm{op}}$, shows that $X$ has at most $\mu$ simplices in total. Since $B$ is precisely its nondegenerate simplices, $|B|\leq\mu<\kappa$. All sets are in $\mathcal U$. This counting argument is not used at $\kappa=\aleph_0$.

source.place: Cardinality audit of HTT Variant 4.2.3.15: its categories of simplices and their nerves use countably many finite-word operations; the smallness convention is def-coef-presentable-infinity-category. Online primary source read 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag is asserted.

proof.text:
It remains to handle $\kappa=\aleph_0$. By the definition in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], $K$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices. Apply [lem-coef-finite-embedded-simplex-resolution] to obtain a finite simplicial set $Q$ and $q:Q\to K$, with all nondegenerate simplices of $Q$ monomorphisms and with $R_q$ a universal equivalence. Apply step 2 with $X=Q$ and put $B=B_Q$. Its objects are exactly the nondegenerate simplices of $Q$, so $B$ is finite, including the possible empty case. By [lem-coef-simplex-last-vertex-cocone-equivalence], the map $\ell_Q:N(\mathsf S(Q))\to Q$ has universal restriction equivalences. Define
$$\varphi=q\circ\ell_Q\circ N(i_Q):N(B)\longrightarrow K.$$
Its restriction map is the composite $R_{N(i_Q)}R_{\ell_Q}R_q$, so steps 1 and 2 give exactly the displayed equivalence in the item. This uses a finite resolution before forming the face poset; the countably infinite degeneracy category itself is never claimed finite.

source.place: HTT Variant 4.2.3.16, printed p. 256: claim (*′) followed by the face-poset argument in the first paragraph. Online primary source read 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag is asserted.

proof.text: For either cardinal case the constructed $B$ and $\varphi$ depend on $K$ and satisfy the equivalence for EVERY $\mathcal E,p,T$. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] the two mapping simplicial sets are Kan. An equivalence of these spaces is surjective on components by the weak-homotopy-equivalence convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Given a vertex representing a prescribed cocone on $p\varphi$, choose a source vertex whose image represents its component; the two target vertices are joined by a path in that Kan space. This proves the final cocone assertion. All inputs were restriction equivalences or comma tests, which required no colimits in $\mathcal E$.
